newsitem.title: JAPAN: Japan committee passes forex deregulation bill.
newsitem.headline: Japan committee passes forex deregulation bill.

text.p: A key Japanese parliamentary committee on Thursday approved a bill to ease foreign exchange controls that will liberalise the foreign exchange business and enable freer cross-border capital transactions.
The bill is now expected to be passed into law by parliament's Upper House on Friday. The provisions will take effect from April 1988, parliamentary officials said.

The liberalisation of foreign exchange controls is in the vanguard of Prime Minister Ryutaro Hashimoto's "Big Bang" financial reforms, which aim to bring Japan's financial markets into line with other world centres by the year 2001.
The revision to the law will allow firms to transfer capital overseas without the help of banks, by abolishing rules which now limit foreign exchange business to authorised banks.
This is expected to lower the cost and currency risks for companies involved in such transactions.
Companies and individuals will also be allowed to open bank accounts overseas and will be able to change yen into foreign currency freely within Japan.

However, analysts have said that if controls on foreign exchange transactions are lifted without deregulation being carried out in areas such as taxes, it could prompt an exodus of Japanese capital to overseas markets.

The committee's support for the bill was conditional on the government agreeing to consider appropriate measures to deal with money laundering and illegal transactions, and to consider revising certain taxes, parliamentary officials said.
